# Problem 0

## Loading All Libraries

```{r loading_libraries, message = F}
# loading tidyverse library
library(tidyverse)

# loading p8105.datasets library
library(p8105.datasets)

# loading patchworks library
library(patchwork)
```


# Problem 1

## Reading ny_noaa dataset

```{r reading_p1_data, message = F}
# reading ny_noaa data
data("ny_noaa")
```

## Short Description

The `ny_noaa` has `r nrow(ny_noaa)` rows and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` columns. Its key (column) variables include `r paste(names(ny_noaa), collapse = ", ")`. The variables have the following data types, respectively: `r paste(sapply(ny_noaa, class), collapse = ", ")`. As for what each variable represents: `id` gives the weather station ID, 
`date` gives the date of observation, `prcp` gives precipitation in tenths of mm, `snow` gives snowfall in mm, `snwd` gives snow depth in mm, `tmax` gives maximum temperature in tenths of degrees C, and `tmin` gives minimum temperature in tenths of degrees C. The proportion of missing values in each column is approximately as follows: `r ny_noaa |> summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)) |> round(2) |> paste0("%", collapse = ", ")`. To clean the data, the missing values should be standardized to `NA`.

## Cleaning ny_noaa Data

```{r ny_noaa_data_cleaning, message = F}
# creating, cleaning and standardizing values in ny_noaa_df
ny_noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = as.numeric(prcp) / 10
  )

# counting the most commonly observed values for snowfall
ny_noaa_df |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```

## Interpretating the Cleaned ny_noaa Data

In the `ny_noaa_df`, `r ny_noaa |> summarize(median_snow = median(snow, na.rm = TRUE))`mm is the most commonly observed value because it does not snow throughout most of the year in New York.

## Plotting Avg. Max Temp. in January and in July in each Station over Years

```{r temp_two_panel_plot, message = FALSE}
#  calculating average maximum temperature for each station, year, and month
avg_max_temp =
  ny_noaa_df |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = as.numeric(month)
  ) |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax))

# creating a two-panel plot comparing January and July temperatures
avg_max_temp |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_tmax,
    group = id,
    color = month
  )) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    color = "Month"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

##  Comments on Structure and Outliers
Yes, there is an observable/interpretable structure. The July maximum average temperatures are consistently higher than the January ones. The is a pattern that is seasonally expected. Temperatures also vary across stations and years, though, there is a visible overall pattern to the data across time in each plot. There are some potential outliers in each where some stations appear to be experiencing unusually high or low average maximum temperatures relative to the general set.


```{r range_two_panel_plot, message =F}
# plotting tmax vs tmin for the full dataset
temp_range_plot =
  ny_noaa_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_bin2d(na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs. Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    fill = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# plotting distribution of snowfall values > 0 and <100 separately by year
snowfall_range_plot =
  ny_noaa_df |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year)) |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))

# combining into a two-panel plot
temp_range_plot + snowfall_range_plot
```
